stem.en: In a planned economy, the yearly plan fixes umbrella production at 10,000 and the price at ₹120. This monsoon, buyers want twice as many umbrellas as planned. What is most likely to happen in the shops?

text.en: Unsold umbrellas pile up, because the plan always makes too many.
The price rises to ₹240 by itself, so fewer people buy.
Quality improves quickly, as factories race to win new buyers.
Umbrellas run out, since the number and price are both fixed.

explanation.en: The plan fixes both how many umbrellas are made and their price, so the extra buyers cannot be served: the shops run out until the next plan (d). Twice the buyers cannot leave a pile of unsold umbrellas (a). The price cannot change without the plan (b). With fixed targets and few rivals, factories have little reason to improve (c).

hints.en: The plan fixes two things: the number of umbrellas and the price.
